# Legend

> What a chart's colours mean: a small square of each, its name and, if it helps, its value, in a row that wraps.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/legend/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/legend.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | node |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: A `<ul>`: the items in a row, 16px apart, wrapping when there's no room.
- `item`: An `<li>`: the square, the name and the value, 6px apart.
- `swatch`: An 8px square with 2px corners, in BarChart's grey.
- `current-swatch`: The same square in BarChart's green.
- `label`: Label type, in the secondary text colour.
- `value` (optional): Label type, medium weight, the main text colour.

## When to use

- **Under a chart.** Under a BarChart, saying that green is this month and grey the ones before, with this month's total.

## When not to use

- **One colour.** A chart with one colour needs a title, not a legend.

## Behaviour

It lists what each colour means, in the order the chart uses them. It doesn't draw the chart or know about it.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<ul>`; the squares are drawing, hidden from screen readers, so each item reads as its name and value.
- **Colour**: The names are 11:1 and the values 17:1 on the dark page. The squares are 4.3:1 and 10:1.

## Content

Name what the colour stands for (This month, Earlier), not the colour.
